motivation: In recognition of his significant and exact contributions to quantum field theory and its application to quantum electrodynamics, phase transitions, disordered systems and the fractional quantum Hall effect.
In recognition of his significant and fundamental contributions to general relativity, cosmology and general relativistic kinetic theory and hydrodynamics.
In recognition of his significant contributions to the quantum theory of transition metals and in particular to the semiclassical relation (trace formula) between periodic orbits and quantum spectra.

For his significant contributions to quantum field theory and laser physics, as well as for his work in the field of neuroscience; since the 1970s he has researched the information processing of the human brain, in particular the interplay of vision, the sense of movement and eye movement. This neural coordination fails in people with balance disorders; in seasickness sufferers, too, it is out of rhythm.

For his significant contributions to the field of quantum optics, in particular the interaction of laser light with atoms; of particular note are his works on ultracold bosonic gases in optical lattices and on achieving long coherence times in quantum computers.

For his significant contributions to the theory of condensed matter, in particular to the development of mode-coupling theory and its successful application to the understanding of the glass transition.

For his significant contributions to the statistical physics of equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems, in particular for his contributions to the theory of phase transitions, the dynamics of infinite systems and stationary states in non-equilibrium; he is further honored for being at the forefront of new trends in the field and for introducing several generations of scientists to it with great enthusiasm.
For his outstanding contributions to quantum field theory.

For his very significant contributions to the fields of quantum optics, the statistical mechanics of open stationary systems outside thermodynamic equilibrium, quantum fluids and quantum gases, and quantum chaos, as well as his treatment of quantum aspects of cosmology.

In recognition of his significant contributions to the derivation of a new mean-field theory of correlated quantum systems and to the understanding of many-body problems in the quantum theory of condensed matter.

For his significant contributions to theoretical elementary particle physics and quantum field theory and to statistical physics, in particular of systems with quenched disorder, above all spin glasses.

For his significant contributions to linking supersymmetry and random matrices and their applications in nuclei, disordered mesoscopic systems and chaotic quantum systems, as well as to other areas of mathematical physics.
For his important work on magnetic monopole solutions in Yang-Mills theories and his classification of the modular partition functions important for string theories and of the super Lie algebras.
For his fundamental contributions to relativistic quantum field theory, statistical mechanics and the theory of dynamical systems, with applications to the problem of the onset of turbulence.
In recognition of his fundamental contributions to cosmology, in particular to structure formation from quantum fluctuations in the early universe.
In recognition of his fundamental contributions to the theory of phase transitions - in particular in low-dimensional magnetic systems - and to the dynamics of critical phenomena.
In recognition of his significant contributions to statistical physics in elucidating the transition from microscopic physics to macroscopic behavior.
For his outstanding contributions in the field of quantum information theory and quantum optics.
In recognition of his significant theoretical contributions to the understanding of single-bubble sonoluminescence and to the physics of turbulent flows.
For his outstanding contributions to applied quantum field theory of the fundamental interactions, in particular in the field of flavor physics and quantum chromodynamics.

In recognition of his groundbreaking pioneering work on quantum field theory and statistical mechanics, in particular on monopoles and instanton solutions of Yang-Mills theories, the conformal bootstrap and gauge-string duality.

In recognition of her fundamental contributions, which have had a lasting conceptual and methodological influence on the statistical physics of condensed matter; in particular for her outstanding work on the melting transitions of thin films, the statistical theory of neural networks and the dynamics of granular gases.

In recognition of his numerous and fundamental contributions to relativistic astrophysics and to cosmology, in particular for the theoretical prediction of experimentally observed changes in the spectrum of cosmic background radiation passing through galaxy clusters.
In recognition of his fundamental contributions to theoretical biophysics, in particular to intercellular transport, biomolecular processes and pattern formation in complex systems.
In recognition of his fundamental theoretical contributions to quantum entanglement, quantum non-locality and the field of quantum information.

In recognition of his groundbreaking contributions to the simulation of microscopic models of polymers, which clarified theoretical questions in polymer physics and provided indispensable tools for materials science.
